observation_summary: The NumberUtils.createNumber method incorrectly parses floating-point strings as Float even when they exceed the precision capacity of a Float, leading to truncation and loss of precision.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces conditional checks (if(numDecimals <= 7) and if(numDecimals <= 16)) to validate whether a string can be safely represented as a Float or Double before attempting the conversion. This is a classic case of missing validation logic (a guard) that determines which path the algorithm should take to ensure data integrity. It is not an algorithmic rewrite of the conversion itself, but rather a missing check on the input data's characteristics to decide the appropriate target type.
evidence_used: The fix adds 'if(numDecimals <= 7)' and 'if(numDecimals <= 16)' guards before attempting Float and Double conversions.
The bug report states that the method always tries to parse as Float first, causing truncation for numbers that require higher precision.
The fix ensures that the method only attempts to create a Float or Double if the number of decimal places is within the precision limits of those types.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic flow is modified, the core issue is the lack of a validation check (guard) to determine if the input is suitable for the chosen type, rather than a flaw in the conversion algorithm itself.
